external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third party that settles payments and sends a webhook indicating that an order is paid.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: The internet-exposed Node service through which shoppers browse and place orders, and which receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: Shopper accounts use email and password with a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out.

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that receives orders from the storefront API, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service uses a single application account with full read/write access.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive
data_stores.notes: Each receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: browse and place orders
data_flows.description: A shopper browses the storefront and submits orders to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.notes: Shopper authentication uses email and password and a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out.
data_flows.data_description: Browsing requests, sign-in credentials, session cookie, and order submissions

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in the orders database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The application account password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment to indicate that the order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: Payment-settlement notification that an order is paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network where the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

assumptions.assumption: The orders database is confidential because it contains shopper addresses, card-last-four values, and order records.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values live in orders-db.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is confidential because it contains completed-order receipt records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order produces a receipt in the receipt archive.
